mainTopic: Where and when שלמים may be slaughtered: the dispute over the three פסוקים, the rule that the היכל entrance must be open, and how openings made the whole עזרה valid
overview: The גמרא explains what the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר argue about. Each of them uses the three פסוקים about where שלמים are slaughtered differently: the תנא קמא learns צפון by logic and uses a פסוק to rule out the צידי צדדים, while רבי אליעזר needs a פסוק for צפון. Next the גמרא asks why one פסוק says 'פתח אהל מועד' instead of 'לפני אהל מועד'. It answers that שלמים slaughtered before the doors of the היכל open are פסולין, and adds that in the משכן they are פסולין if slaughtered before it was set up or after it was taken down. The גמרא then asks what counts as a closed entrance. A shut door counts as closed, but a curtain does not. A proof about a tall obstruction, from two small doors in the בית החליפות, is pushed off, and the details of those doors are defended. Finally, a small niche behind the בית הכפורת made the back of the עזרה valid too, hinted at by the פסוק 'שנים לפרבר'. The amud ends as שמואל begins a new rule about entering the מקדש in טומאה, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: What is the disagreement really about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the underlying point of dispute is between the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר in the ברייתא about where שלמים may be slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: With regard to what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the two opinions in the ברייתא are really arguing about. This question sets up the next two steps, which explain each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים work from the same פסוקים, yet they reach different results. The גמרא wants to find exactly where their readings split.

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: 'They' means the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר from the ברייתא the גמרא just quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the analysis of the ברייתא quoted just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying point of dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: How the first opinion uses the three verses
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא reads three פסוקים: one for the basic requirement of פתח אהל מועד, one to make the צדדים valid, and one to make the צידי צדדים invalid. He needs no פסוק to make צפון valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא holds that three פסוקים are written. One teaches the basic rule that slaughter must be at the entrance of the אהל מועד. One makes the sides valid. One disqualifies the sides of the sides. No פסוק is needed to make the north valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the תנא קמא assigns a job to each of the three פסוקים about שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק gives the basic location, opposite the entrance. The second widens it to the צדדים, the rest of the courtyard area eastward from the entrance. The third shuts out the צידי צדדים, the parts not in front of the entrance at all. צפון does not need a פסוק because it can be learned by logic (a קל וחומר).

keyTerms.meaning: The first (unnamed) opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
The entrance of the Tent of Meeting
The sides: courtyard areas eastward from the entrance, not only directly in front of it
The sides of the sides: areas not in front of the entrance at all

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:
three verses are written;
one for its own point:
that we require the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,
and one to make the sides valid,
and one to disqualify the sides of the sides.
And the north did not need a verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: תְּלָתָא קְרָאֵי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 1 for the תנא קמא's side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three פסוקים teach: the basic requirement, valid צדדים, and invalid צידי צדדים. צפון needs no פסוק.

steps.title: How רבי אליעזר uses the three verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads the three פסוקים as: the basic requirement, making צפון valid, and making the צדדים valid. He needs no פסוק about the צידי צדדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds that one פסוק teaches the basic rule of slaughtering at the entrance of the אהל מועד. One makes the north valid. One makes the sides valid. No פסוק is needed for the sides of the sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אליעזר's side: he uses the same three פסוקים, but gives the second and third different jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the תנא קמא, רבי אליעזר does not learn צפון by logic. He needs a פסוק to make it valid. Because of that, he has no פסוק left for the צידי צדדים, and he holds that point does not need its own פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The north side of the courtyard

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree there are three פסוקים and that the first teaches the basic rule. They argue over whether צפון needs a פסוק (רבי אליעזר) or the צידי צדדים need one (תנא קמא).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer holds:
one for its own point:
that we require the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,
and one to make the north valid,
and one to make the sides valid.
And the sides of the sides did not need a verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to step 1 by giving רבי אליעזר's reading, in contrast to step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three פסוקים teach: the basic requirement, valid צפון, and valid צדדים. The צידי צדדים need no פסוק.

steps.title: Why does one verse say 'entrance' and the others 'before'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ויקרא 3:2 says 'פתח אהל מועד' while the other פסוקים say 'לפני אהל מועד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different here, that it is written 'the entrance of the Tent of Meeting', and what is different there, that it is written 'before the Tent of Meeting'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a change in wording between the פסוקים and asks what the different wording teaches. The next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all three פסוקים are about the place of slaughter, why use two different phrases? The גמרא assumes the word 'פתח' (entrance) must be teaching something extra.

phrases.english: What is different here,
that it is written: 'the entrance of the Tent of Meeting',
and what is different there,
that it is written: 'before the Tent of Meeting'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דִּכְתִיב פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how the פסוקים are divided up to why their wording differs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'פתח' adds that 'לפני' does not.

steps.title: The entrance must be open when slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The word 'פתח' teaches the rule of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: שלמים slaughtered before the doors of the היכל were opened are פסולין, because slaughter must be done when the entrance is open.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us the rule of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: שלמים that were slaughtered before the doors of the היכל were opened are invalid. The פסוק says 'and he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the אהל מועד', which means when it is open, and not when it is locked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'פתח' teaches a new rule: the entrance must actually be open when the שלמים are slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לפני' just tells us the location. 'פתח' means an entrance, and a locked door is not working as an entrance. So if the היכל doors are still closed, slaughtering שלמים makes them פסולין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a rule about timing, not just place: in the בית המקדש, שלמים may not be slaughtered until the היכל doors are open.

phrases.english: It teaches us
like what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel;
for Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
Peace offerings that one slaughtered
before the doors of the Sanctuary were opened are disqualified,
as it says: 'And he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting',
when it is open,
and not when it is locked.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'פתח' teaches that the entrance must be open; שלמים slaughtered before the היכל doors are opened are פסולין.

steps.title: A second אמורא says the same rule
steps.stepSummary: The same rule was also said by מר עוקבא בר חמא in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: שלמים slaughtered before the doors of the היכל open are פסולין, based on 'פתח אהל מועד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: מר עוקבא בר חמא said in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: שלמים slaughtered before the doors of the היכל were opened are invalid. The פסוק says 'and he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the אהל מועד', meaning when the entrance of the היכל is open, and not when it is locked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a matching statement from another אמורא to back up שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling and the פסוק are the same as in step 5. The only difference is that this version spells out that 'the entrance' means the entrance of the היכל.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (a matching ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'פתח' teaches that שלמים may only be slaughtered while the היכל doors are open. If slaughtered before, they are פסולין. Two separate אמוראים teach this.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Mar Ukva bar Ḥama said
in the name of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina:
Peace offerings that one slaughtered
before the doors of the Sanctuary were opened are disqualified,
as it says: 'And he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting',
when the entrance of the Sanctuary is open,
and not when it is locked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 5 with a parallel statement from another אמורא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that שלמים slaughtered before the היכל doors open are פסולין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, passed on by מר עוקבא בר חמא.

steps.title: The version taught in the West, with an added law for the משכן
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they taught the rule in the name of רב יעקב בר אחא from רב אשי. It adds that in the משכן, שלמים slaughtered before the לויים set it up or after they took it down are פסולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West they teach it like this: רב יעקב בר אחא said in the name of רב אשי: שלמים slaughtered before the doors of the היכל were opened are invalid. And in the משכן, if they were slaughtered before the לויים set up the משכן, or after the לויים took the משכן apart, they are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third version of the same rule, the one taught in ארץ ישראל. This version adds a law about the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משכן had no doors that could be opened or shut. So this version explains what 'open' means there: the משכן has to be standing. Before it is set up or after it is taken down, there is no open entrance, and the שלמים are פסולים.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
The Levites, who set up and took down the משכן

phrases.english: In the West they teach it like this:
phrases.notes: The West here means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Ya'akov bar Acha said in the name of Rav Ashi:
Peace offerings that one slaughtered
before the doors of the Sanctuary were opened are invalid.

phrases.aramaic: וּבַמִּשְׁכָּן – קוֹדֶם שֶׁיַּעֲמִידוּ לְוִיִּם אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן,
phrases.english: And in the Tabernacle: before the Levites set up the Tabernacle,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְאַחַר שֶׁיְּפָרְקוּ לְוִיִּם אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן – פְּסוּלִים.
phrases.english: or after the Levites took the Tabernacle apart, they are invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the rule from steps 5 and 6, with a different chain of names and an added law about the משכן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמים slaughtered before the היכל doors open are פסולים. In the משכן, they are פסולים if slaughtered before it was set up or after it was taken down.

steps.title: A shut door counts as locked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is obvious that a door that is shut but not locked counts as closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that a shut door is treated like a locked one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the easy case first: a shut door counts as closed. This sets up the harder questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A door does not need to be locked to make the entrance closed. If the door is shut, the entrance is not open, so שלמים slaughtered then would be פסולים.

phrases.english: It is obvious: a shut door is like a locked one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins working out what counts as an open or closed entrance under the rule just taught.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shut door counts as closed, the same as a locked door.

steps.title: What about a curtain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a curtain hanging over the entrance makes it count as closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law if there is a curtain?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks about a harder case: a curtain hanging in the entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A curtain blocks the view the way a door does, but it is easy to push aside. So it is unclear whether it counts as closing the entrance.

phrases.english: A curtain, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the clear case of a shut door to the unclear case of a curtain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a curtain over the entrance make it count as closed?

steps.title: A curtain is like an open entrance
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that a curtain is only made to be used like an open entrance, so it does not close it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: A curtain itself is made only to act like an open entrance.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question about the curtain. It does not count as closing the entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A door is made to shut the entrance. A curtain is made for an entrance that people walk through. So the entrance behind it is still treated as open, and שלמים slaughtered then are valid.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
It itself is not made
except to act like an open entrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: הוּא עַצְמוֹ אֵין נַעֲשֶׂה אֶלָּא כְּפֶתַח פָּתוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the curtain question from step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A curtain does not close the entrance. It is treated like an open entrance.

steps.title: What about something tall blocking the entrance?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a tall obstruction standing in front of the entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law about something tall?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question: what if something tall stands in front of the entrance? This opens the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The door is open, but a tall object blocks the way in front of it. The question is whether that blocking makes the entrance count as closed.

phrases.english: Something tall, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means a tall object standing in front of an open entrance and blocking it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the curtain, the גמרא asks about another kind of blocking.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a tall obstruction in front of an open entrance make it count as closed?

steps.title: A ברייתא about two small doors in the Chamber
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: there were two small doors in the בית החליפות, eight אמות high. They made the whole עזרה valid for eating קדשי קדשים and slaughtering קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: There were two small doors in the בית החליפות, and their height was eight. Their purpose was to make the whole עזרה fit for eating קדשי קדשים and for slaughtering קדשים קלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question about the tall obstruction. Here it only quotes the source; the next step shows how it is supposed to prove the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These small doors opened the back area of the עזרה to the היכל side, so that area also counted as being in front of the entrance. That is why the whole עזרה became valid for these קרבנות. The words 'eight high' are what the גמרא will try to use as the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The Chamber of Knives in the בית המקדש
קרבנות of lesser holiness, such as שלמים

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
There were two small doors in the Chamber of Knives,
and their height was eight,
phrases.notes: Eight אמות. The next step argues over what exactly was eight high.

phrases.english: in order to make the entire courtyard fit
for eating offerings of the highest holiness,
and for slaughtering offerings of lesser holiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to try to answer the question about something tall.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a tall obstruction makes an entrance count as closed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה about two small doors in the בית החליפות

steps.title: Reading 'eight' as a tall blocking in front
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'eight' means something eight high stood in front of the small doors, and the area still counted as open.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, does it not mean that there was something eight high in front of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the ברייתא would prove the point. It suggests that 'eight' refers to a tall barrier in front of the doors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If something eight אמות high stood in front of the doors and the עזרה was still valid, then a tall obstruction does not close an entrance. That would answer the question from step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: What, does it not mean, introducing a suggested reading

phrases.english: What, does it not mean that there was something eight high in front of them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the ברייתא from step 12 would prove the point.
steps.raayaObject: A tall obstruction does not make an entrance count as closed
steps.raayaSupportSource: Reading 'eight' in the ברייתא as an eight-high barrier in front of the doors

steps.title: No: the doors themselves were eight high
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. 'Eight' means the small doors themselves were eight אמות tall, not that something stood in front of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: No; it means that their own height was eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. 'Eight' only describes how tall the small doors were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'eight' is just the height of the doors, the ברייתא says nothing about a barrier in front of them. So it cannot prove anything about a tall obstruction, and the question from step 11 is left without a proof here.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as a ruling that a tall obstruction closes the entrance. The גמרא only shows that this ברייתא does not prove the opposite.

phrases.english: No; it is their own height that was eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא given in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא only. It gives no ruling of its own on the question about something tall.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Eight' can be read as the height of the small doors themselves, not a barrier in front of them.

steps.title: All gates in the Temple were twenty cubits tall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the small doors were eight אמות tall, because a משנה says every gate there was twenty אמות high and ten wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: All the gates that were there were twenty cubits high and ten cubits wide!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the conclusion of Step 14. A משנה says all the gates in the מקדש were twenty אמות high, so how could these small doors be only eight?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said the small doors themselves were eight אמות tall. This משנה gives one size for every gate, which seems to rule out an eight-אמה doorway. So the reading from Step 14 looks wrong.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
All the gates that were there,
their height was twenty cubits,
and their width was ten cubits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in Step 14 that the small doors were eight אמות tall.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the small doors themselves were eight אמות high.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says every gate in the מקדש was twenty אמות high, so an eight-אמה door seems impossible.

steps.title: Small doors are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the twenty-אמה rule is about real gates, not small side doors.
steps.simpleTranslation: Small doors are different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the משנה is talking about full gates, and small doors do not count as gates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of twenty אמות covers the main gates only. פשפשין are a different kind of opening, so they can be eight אמות. That keeps Step 14 in place.

phrases.english: Small doors are different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between categories (gates vs. small doors).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every opening in the מקדש had to be twenty אמות tall.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only real gates were twenty אמות. Small doors could be eight.

steps.title: What about the side areas?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the small doors could make the whole עזרה valid, since some side areas would not face them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the sides!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the ברייתא of Step 12. The small doors faced one direction, so how could they help the areas off to the sides?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the two small doors made the whole עזרה valid. But places on the sides of the בית החליפות would not be facing those doors. So it seems the doors cannot cover the whole עזרה.

phrases.english: But there are the sides!
phrases.notes: He means the areas off to the sides, which do not face the small doors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new difficulty with the ברייתא of Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the small doors made the whole עזרה valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Doors facing one way cannot serve the areas to the sides.

steps.title: The doors were set at the corners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the small doors were placed at the corners, so they faced the side areas too.
steps.simpleTranslation: They set them in at the corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the small doors were built into the corners, so they opened toward the sides as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because each door was placed at a corner, it faced at an angle and covered the side area too. So the two doors together could serve the whole עזרה.

phrases.english: That they set them in at the corner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of Step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doors faced straight out and did not serve the side areas.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doors sat in the corners, so they served the sides too.

steps.title: What about the area behind the Holy of Holies?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the area behind the בית הכפורת counted as facing an opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about behind the Hall of the Ark Cover?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question: what makes the area behind the בית הכפורת valid, since it does not face any entrance?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main entrance and the small doors cannot be seen from behind the building. So the גמרא wants to know how that part of the עזרה could be used for eating קדשי קדשים and slaughtering קדשים קלים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Hall of the Ark Cover (the קודש הקדשים)

phrases.english: What about the area behind the Hall of the Ark Cover?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the side areas to the area behind the building.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the area behind the בית הכפורת counts as facing an opening.

steps.title: A small niche stood behind the Holy of Holies
steps.stepSummary: רב says there was a small niche eight אמות high behind the בית הכפורת, made to make the whole עזרה valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רמי בר רב יהודה said in the name of רב: There was a small niche behind the Hall of the Ark Cover, eight cubits high, to make the courtyard valid for eating the most holy offerings and for slaughtering the lesser offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with רב's teaching. There was a small niche (לול) behind the בית הכפורת, built to serve as an opening for that area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לול gave the back area its own opening to face. Like the small doors, it was eight אמות high. Because of it, the back of the עזרה was also valid for eating קדשי קדשים and slaughtering קדשים קלים.

phrases.english: Come and hear,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: for Rami bar Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: לוּל קָטָן הָיָה אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכַּפּוֹרֶת,
phrases.english: There was a small niche behind the Hall of the Ark Cover,
eight cubits high;
in order to make the courtyard valid
for eating the most holy offerings,
and for slaughtering the offerings of lesser holiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A small eight-אמה niche behind the בית הכפורת served as an opening for that area.

steps.title: A verse hints at the niche
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רב's teaching with the פסוק "two at the פרבר".
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: "Two at the פרבר."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from דברי הימים that it reads as pointing to this niche at the back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists guards placed at the western side, including "two at the פרבר". The גמרא connects that spot to the niche behind the בית הכפורת. The meaning of the word פרבר is explained in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written
A word in the פסוק, explained next

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"Two at the parbar."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a פסוק as support for רב's teaching in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The existence of the niche behind the בית הכפורת.

steps.title: What does 'פרבר' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word פרבר in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "לפרבר" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the unusual word פרבר means, since the proof depends on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from the פסוק only works if פרבר fits the idea of an opening at the back. So the גמרא needs to explain the word.

phrases.english: What is "laparbar"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the פסוק of Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word פרבר.

steps.title: פרבר means facing outward
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא explains that פרבר is like saying "toward the outside".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא said: It is like one who says "facing outward."
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב שילא explains the word: פרבר sounds like כלפי בר, "toward the outside."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading פרבר as "facing out" fits an opening at the back that faces outward. This ties the פסוק to the niche behind the בית הכפורת.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole עזרה counted as facing an opening: the main entrance, the two small doors set in the corners, and a small eight-אמה niche behind the בית הכפורת.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Sheila said:
It is like one who says: Facing outward.
phrases.notes: The word פרבר sounds like כלפי בר, "toward the outside."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא, כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר: כְּלַפֵּי בַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרבר means facing outward, fitting an outward-facing opening at the back.

steps.title: When one is liable for entering in impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל begins a new rule: one is liable for entering in טומאה only for a certain area.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that שמואל said: One is liable for impurity only for...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רב יהודה quotes שמואל about where a person is liable for entering in טומאה, and the sentence continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "only" tells us שמואל is limiting the liability to one specific area. Which area that is comes in the continuation.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
One is not liable because of impurity,
phrases.notes: He means entering the מקדש area while impure.

phrases.english: except for
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching, separate from the discussion of the openings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for entering in טומאה is limited to a specific area (given in the continuation).
